podcast.body: The debut single by The Specials from 1979 notably features singer Terry Hall saying, "Bernie Rhodes don't argue" at the beginning. This shout-out is a direct reference to Bernie Rhodes, who was the band's manager. The line refers to an incident at a Paris hotel where management confiscated the Specials' gear due to non-payment, and Bernie was entangled in the situation.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This track initiated the "second wave" of ska and notably featured a sample from a song by first-wave ska master Prince Buster. "And appropriately, it all started with an actual sample from a song written by a first wave skommaster named Prince Buster. The track is gangsters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the very first record released by The Specials on Jerry Dammers' Two-tone label in May 1979. 5,000 copies were sent out, and the song reached number six on the British charts, which was an unprecedented achievement for an indie record at the time. "5,000 copies were sent out in May 1979 and this song reached number six on the British charts. That never ever happened with an indie record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
